scenario: [LCCO.8.3.2]: an `error <pattern>:` continuation matches a CallError whose code's segments start with the pattern's, at segment boundaries, not by character prefix. Three Req facts a, b, c each issue one call, correlated `c-<id>`; each call is answered by a CallError with its own code: a `adapter` (the pattern itself), b `adapter.failed` (a longer code under it), c `adapterx` (a character prefix, not a segment). The rule's only continuation is `error adapter:`, and it logs the request's id. Each CallError is asserted and pumped on its own, so the order is the order of the answers: exactly ["adapter a", "adapter b"]. A runtime matching by character prefix also logs c; one matching only the exact code drops b. A code that differs after `_` (`adapter_failed`) is logical/LCCO.8.3.2_underscore_is_not_a_boundary's. The compile side is compiler/LCCO.8.3.2 and compiler/LECC.6.2a; this is the runtime half. [LECC.6.4] admits `adapter`.
rules_ds:
service svc.read:
    kwarg entity_id: String
    no response

schema Req scope logical:
    id: String key

rule r:
    Req q
->
    call svc.read entity_id: q.id nocooldown as "c-{q.id}"
        error adapter:
            log info "adapter {q.id}"
